text:
maya: heads up — we saw a bunch of GPU scale-ups fail in us-west-2 over the last 20m. apps queued but Karpenter didn't register new nodes

ravi: ugh, logs?

maya: paste from karpenter-controller: 
`E0908 12:34:21.123 controller.go:422] provisioner/provision failed: LaunchInstances failed: InvalidLaunchTemplateName.NotFound`

maya: also a bunch of nodes came up with the older AMI so they didn't have the nvidia-driver label, and the gpu-scheduler is ignoring them

julia: so two separate issues: launch template drift + AMI mismatch. are we still relying on managed nodepool LT for Karpenter bootstrapping?

sam: we had a temp LT until the new Bottlerocket AMI bake finished, maybe the LT got deleted during the Canary update 

kevin: noticed increased ENI allocation errors earlier too, could be simultaneous region capacity / ENI exhaustion making Karpenter retry different instance types and hit the LT gap

maya: sequence from metrics: surge in pending pods -> provisioner webhook triggers -> attempt to Launch with LT X -> 404 -> fallback attempts -> some instances launched with legacy AMI Y -> taint mismatch -> pods pending 

ravi: quick mitigation: pin the provisioner to an explicit amiSelector for the correct GPU AMI until LT is fixed. e.g.
```
apiVersion: provisioning.karpenter.sh/v1beta1
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-provisioner-locked
spec:
  requirements:
    - key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-gpu
      operator: Exists
  provider:
    amiSelector:
      name: "redwood-gpu-ami-*"
    subnetSelector:
      matchLabels:
        karpenter.k8s.aws/cluster: redwood-prod
  ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 300
```

julia: that will force the right AMI but be careful — if the AMI tag isn't present for a new bake, it will fail-to-provision entirely. I prefer a slide-in: create a stable LT in account and reference it in provider.launchTemplate

sam: we can also set `disruption` constraints: `startupTimeoutSeconds: 300` and `consolidation: disabled` during the roll to avoid premature scale-in oscillation

kevin: good call. also add `taints: gpu=true:NoSchedule` on provisioner and make sure the kube-scheduler predicate matches so legacy nodes don't get targeted

maya: any short-term rollout plan? ops: create LT pointing to current AMI, update Karpenter provisioner provider.launchTemplate, then lift consolidation/ttl once stable

ravi: I'll open a small runbook: create LT -> patch provisioner -> watch for pod scheduling -> rollback if failures. tagging it with `migration: karpenter-lock`

infra-ci: deploybot: Kaniko/image-build pipeline finished for gpu-ami-bake #372 — AMI id ami-0c1234deadbeef available in us-west-2

julia: once the AMI is baked, we should retire the legacy nodepool. but coordinate with SRE to drain gracefully: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` in staged batches

kevin: note on costs: pinning a launch template with on-demand overrides is safer but ups cost slightly. Consider using spot with fallback to on-demand and set nodeTTL to shorter for cost recovery

maya: action items:
- ravi: runbook + LT create (ETA 30m)
- sam: patch provisioner to reference LT and bump startupTimeout (ETA 15m)
- julia: coordinate drain plan for legacy pool (ETA 2h)
- kevin: monitor ENI quotas & raise cloud support if needed (ETA 30m)

k8s-bot: cluster-alert: GPU scheduling backlog > 200 pods in `us-west-2` — alerting channel: #incidents

maya: thanks — will update channel when done. keeping this thread for postmortem notes :thumbsup:

ravi: quick note for migration playbook: include a section on "autoscaler handshake" — how Karpenter behaves when a separate autoscaling mechanism (nodepool autoscaler) still exists. explicit steps: drain, scale-to-zero nodepool, disable nodepool autoscaler, then enable Karpenter consolidation

julia: yep — and add a small script to verify node labeling (`kubectl get nodes -L nvidia.com/gpu`) and a prometheus alert for AMI mismatches by image id

sam: will add a short `kubectl` check to run after each patch, example: `kubectl get nodes -o wide | awk '/gpu/ {print $1,$6}'`

kevin: after patching we'll keep consolidation disabled for 1h, watch pod backlog and eviction metrics. if stable for 30m, re-enable and let Karpenter consolidate

maya: closing loop: if anyone sees new failures ping me @maya, I'll keep an eye on the pod logs and karpenter-controller logs

infra-ci: runbook created: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/karpenter-ami-fallback (internal link)

maya: thanks all. postmortem later if this reoccurs
